note: The Vietnamese wrapping of the santander_vn book (docs/CLIENT_DATASET_PLAN.md). Each table: value, source; 'giả định' = our assumption, to replace with a cited figure.

cities.source: giả định: where wealthy clients live; Santander's provinces keep their rank and are cut to these shares

scf_classes.source: SCF 2022 summary extract variables (federalreserve.gov/econres/scfindex.htm) grouped into the app's classes

retirement_to.source: giả định: Vietnam has no 401(k)/IRA; a US household's retirement accounts are read as these Vietnamese holdings

multipliers.source: giả định: Vietnamese wealthy households hold more property and gold, fewer funds than US ones; shares are multiplied then renormalised

gold_share.source: giả định: gold as a share of total wealth, drawn per client

jitter.source: giả định: each reuse of an SCF household moves every class share by up to ±10 %

casa_in_deposits_with_td.source: giả định: the part of TCB deposits left in CASA when the client also holds a term deposit

td_tenors.source: giả định: Santander barely shows short terms; tenors (months) and their weights, rates per year

income_yield.source: giả định: yearly income as a share of total wealth, at the median Santander income; scaled by (income / median)^0.5

occupations.source: giả định: by the matched household's business share and the client's age

names.source: common Vietnamese surnames and their rough frequencies (Wikipedia, 'Vietnamese name'); given names: our lists

events.source: giả định: yearly odds of a large outflow in the next 12–18 months, and its size as a share of total wealth
